solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Upon which, catch cold

parts.note: a stand is the thing upon which goods are laid out for sale
read cryptically, a catch is something 'of fish', the haul a trawler lands

explanation.surface: A terse instruction: once something happens, grab a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first three words as a definition of a fishmonger's slab: STAND OF FISH, the thing upon which the catch is laid. Respaced, those letters are a single adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof and unfriendly in manner is described as cold, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Broadcast, like that on the radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than read, so the word is the one heard spoken

parts.note: so means like that, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: Asking whether a broadcast is like that one on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' as a definition means scatter seed, not transmit.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter seed widely by hand is to broadcast it, the farming sense of the word.

clue.text: One in England missing out on defence

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside what remains
missing out means leaving something out, here the word on

parts.note: Albion is an old poetic name for England
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An England side missing out because of its defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in England' looks like a single English player, but 'missing out' and 'in' are separate signals; 'defence' is the courtroom kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere at the time of a crime is a defence in court.

clue.text: Flies partied, buzzing around

indicators.note: moving about in excitement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Insects that partied, buzzing about.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the order of insects that includes the two-winged flies and mosquitoes.

clue.text: Anticipate growth of planes etc, the entire fleet?

parts.note: plane trees and other trees grow together as woodland
the whole lot, all of it

explanation.surface: A forecast of plane manufacture, perhaps for an airline's whole fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planes' suggests aircraft, which 'fleet' supports, but they are plane trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act first to prevent something, getting in ahead of it.

clue.text: Tavern has appeal, do you agree?

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
it means sex appeal, as in 1920s slang 'the It girl'

explanation.surface: A pub with charm, isn't that right?
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang tag question, a slurred 'isn't it', seeking agreement.

clue.text: Flaw in entertaining British artist

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them inside, so one piece goes in another

parts.note: a hole is a flaw or defect

explanation.surface: A flaw in an amusing British painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like an adjective for the artist but signals one piece held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Holbein the Younger was the German-Swiss portrait painter at Henry VIII's court.

clue.text: Name game

definitions.meaning: a label or identifying ... attached to something, as in a name ...
the children's chasing game also called tig or it

explanation.surface: Two bare words, as if asking for a game to be named.
explanation.definitionFit: A label giving a name is a tag, and a playground chasing game is also called tag.

clue.text: Rubbish also is written on top of table in permanent marker?

indicators.note: in a down entry, written on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: tat is rubbish, cheap tasteless stuff
too means also

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: Junk scribbled on a table in indelible ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'permanent marker' suggests a felt-tip pen, but means a person who marks skin permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inks designs permanently into skin is a permanent marker in a playful sense.

clue.text: Pretty decent leader in the throne room?

parts.note: good means decent, of fair quality
the throne is a joke name for the toilet, so the room is the loo
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: A rather fine monarch in his throne room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like 'fairly', qualifying 'decent', but is the definition. LOO is British for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive in appearance, a synonym for pretty or handsome.

clue.text: Secure cages in, for each person controlling hounds

indicators.note: to cage something is to enclose it, so the word for secure holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to secure a prize is to win it
hip means fashionable, in
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Someone locking things away, apparently paid by the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'secure cages in' as one phrase, but 'in' is a piece meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A huntsman's assistant who keeps the pack together with a whip has this title in foxhunting.

clue.text: Header missed in tight draw

indicators.note: a header is the opening letter of a word, and missing it means it is dropped

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, as is blotto

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a header misses, the match ends in a tight draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Header missed' drops the first letter, B, from BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw of numbers, and lotto is a lottery game.

clue.text: First of pints gone in seconds, one can't bend the elbow!

indicators.note: the letter has gone into the word for seconds, sitting inside it

parts.note: trices are instants, as in 'in a trice'

indicators.note: only the opening letter of pints is used

explanation.surface: A pint drained in seconds, and a drinker unable to raise another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bend the elbow' is slang for drinking; the joke is that this muscle straightens the elbow rather than bending it, and its name is singular despite looking plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm extends the elbow joint; the opposing biceps is what flexes it.

clue.text: River insect, slow mover to many watching?

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire
a cricket is a chirping insect

explanation.surface: A river creature crawling past onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the five-day international game being slow-moving to many who watch it.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-day form of the international bat-and-ball game seems sluggish to many spectators.

clue.text: Whistler painting attributed to Turner at first — that's a bloomer

indicators.note: credited to, so the letter is placed alongside the following pieces
only the first letter of the painter's name is wanted

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle, so is a whistler
an oil is a painting done in oils

explanation.surface: An art-world blunder: a Whistler canvas wrongly credited to Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler and Turner are both famous painters, which hides the referee. 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is something that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A clover-like plant with three leaflets flowers, so it is literally a bloomer.

clue.text: Bones in line, like back

indicators.note: back means the letters run backwards

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
as means like, as in 'white as snow'

explanation.surface: Vertebrae lined up along the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ARCAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the triangular bones at the base of the spine, plural of sacrum.

clue.text: Hypocrisy surrounding working issue in agreement

indicators.note: surrounding means one word encloses the others

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk
on means working, as a machine is on
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: Hypocrisy over a working issue, settled in agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts ONSON inside CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being consonant with something means being in harmony or accord with it.

clue.text: Moreover, nation developed at a slowish pace

parts.note: and means moreover, adding a point

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country that grew, and slowly at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges NATION into ANTINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning slightly faster than andante, a moderately slow walking pace.

clue.text: Jerk inside with dad, getting scorned

indicators.note: to jerk is to jolt sharply, shaking the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A jerk in the house with Dad, getting looked down on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult aimed at someone, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated with contempt and regarded as unworthy, the past tense of a verb meaning to scorn.

clue.text: Put a lot in a tin for pets

parts.note: a can is a tin
oodles means a lot

explanation.surface: Instructions to fill a tin with plenty of food for the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like a noun for animals but is a verb, to fondle.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and cuddle amorously is to pet, the slang verb for it.

clue.text: Occasional books inspiring me a bit

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: odd means occasional, as in 'the odd drink'
NT is the New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Occasional reading that inspires the reader a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' literally means breathing in, so it takes a piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap or remnant is a bit of something.

clue.text: Infants pictured playing with umpteen toys, though irascible initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each listed word is taken

explanation.surface: Toddlers shown in a picture with heaps of toys, but grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers the first letters of 'pictured', 'umpteen', 'toys', 'though', 'irascible'; 'playing with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic naked children painted in Renaissance art are these infants, plural of putto.

clue.text: Archbishop in particular put away

parts.note: prim means fussy, particular
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A senior cleric, fussy, tidied away.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior archbishop of a country, as of All England, holds this title.

clue.text: Where brothers are taken care of?

definitions.meaning: monks or friars belong to a religious order
sorted out and arranged properly, all neat

explanation.surface: A question about where siblings are looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a monastic brotherhood are within an order, and something sorted out is arranged properly, all neat and tidy.

clue.text: Run commercial on two lines

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an ad is a commercial
II is the Roman numeral two

explanation.surface: A commercial run across two lines of print.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight lines from the centre of a circle to its edge are its radii, plural of radius.

clue.text: A revolution on the horizon

parts.note: a rising is an uprising, a revolution

explanation.surface: A political revolt said to be looming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the horizon is coming up or emerging, just as the sun does when it comes up.

clue.text: Articles in the mess, alternating

indicators.note: alternating means every other letter is taken from each word

explanation.surface: Things in a mess, swapping back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternating' picks I from 'in', TE from 'the' and MS from 'mess', each word on its own; the blog thinks this unsound.
explanation.definitionFit: Items and articles are both general words for individual things or objects.

clue.text: Card cheat of old

definitions.meaning: the jack in a pack of playing cards
an archaic word for a rogue or dishonest man

explanation.surface: A card sharp from the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack in a deck has this older name, and the same word meant a rogue or swindler.

clue.text: Grease smeared on brown trousers

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across entry, so the rearranged letters follow

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: smeared means spread messily, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oily stains on a mechanic's brown trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smeared' rearranges GREASE into AGREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls or hard-wearing denim work trousers are known by this name.

clue.text: Warmer in Skegness, unusually

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark that it is unusually warm in a chilly seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Skegness is a chilly English seaside resort on the Lincolnshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The star at the centre of the solar system heats the Earth, so it is a warmer.

clue.text: King wrapped up in short skirt

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a tutu is a ballet dancer's skirt

explanation.surface: A monarch bundled up in a little ballet skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of TUTU. 'Wrapped up' refers to the bandages of a mummy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun, often called by a short nickname, was found mummified in bandages.

clue.text: She perhaps is in shorter novel about the origins of diverse peoples

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging
origins are beginnings, so the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A woman appearing in a short novel about the roots of various peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges IN, SHORTER, D and P ('the origins of' diverse peoples); 'about' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun she is a grammatical example of the form used for someone spoken about.
